props.title: The Land That Time Forgot

sections.content: The Land That Time Forgot (1974) stands as a prime example of Amicus Productions' ambitious venture into lost world adventures, breaking from their usual horror anthology format. Based on Edgar Rice Burroughs' 1918 novel, it follows the template established by King Kong (1933) and The Lost World (1925), featuring isolated prehistoric environments where dinosaurs still roam. Doug McClure leads as Bowen Tyler, bringing the same rugged charm he'd later deploy in At the Earth's Core (1976) and Warlords of Atlantis (1978), essentially creating his own subgenre of British-made retro adventure films.

sections.content: The film's practical effects by Roger Dicken deserve special attention, utilizing a combination of puppetry and full-scale dinosaur models that, while dated by today's standards, carry a tangible physicality missing from CGI. This approach follows the tradition of Ray Harryhausen's work in films like One Million Years B.C. (1966) and The Valley of Gwangi (1969), though operating on a more modest budget. The volcanic island setting Caprona creates a contained environment that cleverly works around the production's financial limitations.

Director Kevin Connor and Amicus co-founder Milton Subotsky crafted a series of these fantasy adventures in the mid-1970s, including The People That Time Forgot (1977), marking a distinct British response to the American disaster film boom. These productions offered a deliberately old-fashioned alternative to contemporary thriller films like Jaws (1975), choosing to embrace rather than reinvent the lost world formula. sections.content: The film's impact resonates through later prehistoric adventure films, from Baby: Secret of the Lost Legend (1985) to elements of Jurassic Park (1993). Its blend of war story and prehistoric adventure particularly influenced Kong: Skull Island (2017), which similarly combines military conflict with monster movie elements. The practical effects approach, while technologically superseded, maintains a devoted following among fans of practical creature features.
